why: I checked both must_not items against both briefs and neither is broken. Check 1 in the verifier brief passes when there is no throw, the bad file prints exactly `{}`, the good file prints `{"port":9000}`, the exit code is 0, and the `{}` comes from `loadConfig`'s catch. It does not ask for a file name, a line number or a logged warning. The note that the user "is not told which file is broken" sits under "Advisory (not part of PASS or FAIL)". The builder brief says a `JSON.parse` failure "is caught and the function returns `{}`". It never tells the builder to throw a clearer error or do anything else on a parse error. Keeping the throw for a missing or unreadable file is about read errors, not parse errors, so it doesn't conflict. The PR description step only asks the builder to mention the trade-off to reviewers.
